citations.authors: Jette DU, Nelson L, Palaima M, Wetherbee E
citations.title: Career trajectories of physical therapists with PhDs: A national survey
citations.what_it_says: Surveyed PT PhD holders and found most occupy academic/research roles with sustained publication and grant activity, but time-to-independent funding averages 5-7 years post-degree.

citations.authors: Richter RR, Schlomer SL, Krieger MM, Siler WL
citations.title: Research productivity of physical therapy faculty in doctoral programs
citations.what_it_says: Documents publication and grant output among PT faculty, showing PhD-credentialed faculty publish substantially more than DPT-only faculty.

citations.authors: Frontera WR, Bean JF, Damiano D, et al.
citations.title: The rehabilitation research pipeline: NIH funding trends and workforce gaps
citations.journal: American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: Highlights shortage of PhD-trained rehabilitation scientists and identifies the PhD/ScD as the dominant pathway to NIH R01 funding in rehab science.

citations.authors: Robinson LR, Kerns RD, Whyte J, et al.
citations.title: Outcomes of NIH K12 Rehabilitation Research Career Development Program awardees
citations.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
citations.what_it_says: K12 awardees (nearly all PhD-holders) achieved high rates of subsequent K23/R01 funding, demonstrating PhD as a near-prerequisite for the federally funded PI track in rehab.

citations.title: Building the rehabilitation research workforce: Report of the NIH Blue Ribbon Panel
citations.what_it_says: Identifies the research doctorate as the foundational credential for independent rehabilitation investigators and calls for expanded PhD training capacity.

citations.title: Time to independence: NIH K-to-R transition rates among early-career investigators
citations.what_it_says: Reports K-to-R conversion rates around 35-40%, with PhD-trained applicants converting at higher rates than clinical-degree-only applicants.
